paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: the LORD is the one behind the wins. This chapter piles up victory after victory, and twice the writer stops to tell us who was working: "So the LORD made David victorious wherever he went." (1 Chronicles 18:6, 13) David had a strong army, but the chapter won't let us hand the credit to the army.

Now look at what David does with the gold, silver and bronze he gathers. He doesn't keep it. He dedicates it to the LORD (1 Chronicles 18:11), and the bronze from Hadadezer's cities later becomes the bronze Sea and the pillars Solomon makes (1 Chronicles 18:8). I think that's what it looks like when a man really believes the LORD gave him the win. If the win is a gift, you hold it with open hands.

So what does that mean for you, baker? When something goes right, whether it's a big win or just a day that finally came together, say thank you to the LORD out loud. And when you've got something good in your hands, ask what you can give back to Him. I'll be over here with my one patient oven, giving Him the credit for every single batch.
